question: free_tier.unit has no term for free software that prints no quantity: none is also the unit of records with no free allowance, and unlimited claims an absence that no page states. Should records such as netdisk-pan/openlist and netdisk-pan/cloudreve take a new unit term (for example unmetered), or stay at none with verdict qualifies-with-caveat?
why: 22 usable self-hosted records carry unit none (store at commit 0398f4dc), among them netdisk-pan/cloudreve, ci-cd-runners/woodpecker-selfhost and coding-subs/cline. Rule C01 flags none with verdict qualifies and passes none with qualifies-with-caveat only because free_tier.stated does not begin with a no-free phrase. For OpenList the README, the terms page, the quick start, the FAQ and the configuration page print no allowance and none calls the offer unlimited; the only unlimited or no-limit sentences are the max_connections default of 0, the max_concurrency value 0 and the form upload with no size limit, which are connection, concurrency and upload-size settings and no allowance. netdisk-pan/openlist is proposed at qualifies-with-caveat with unit none
